techniques.summary: Two or three named cursors move and act on the same canvas at the same time, each in its own rhythm, while presence avatars stack in the corner, so collaboration reads without a word.
techniques.use_when: Collaborative documents, whiteboards, design and planning tools: anything whose claim is 'together, live'.
techniques.avoid_when: A single-user product, or a frame where the name flags would be too small to read; never more than three cursors, which turns into noise.

techniques.name: Mark slides aside, name follows
techniques.summary: The centred mark glides sideways, shrinking if it was hero-sized, to open its slot, and the name resolves beside it just before the mark stops, so the lockup forms in one gesture.
techniques.use_when: Any end card whose mark is already on screen (it was the story device or the hero) and the name still has to arrive. The default lockup build.
techniques.avoid_when: The mark has not been seen yet (give it its own beat first). The film already used a slide-to-make-room for the product. Long names that would push the slide past ~400 px (stack vertically instead).

techniques.name: Name types backwards, group stays centred
techniques.summary: The name appears from its last letter to its first while the mark is pushed outward, so the lockup grows out of the mark's edge and stays centred on every frame.
techniques.use_when: Agent, assistant or persona products whose mark is an avatar or a disc. Names of 4-12 characters. A centred lockup that must never jump.
techniques.avoid_when: Two-word names whose second word makes no sense on its own first. Right-to-left scripts (it becomes an ordinary type-on). The headline already used a typewriter.

techniques.name: Pull out of the mark, undershoot, breathe
techniques.summary: The mark arrives so large that only fragments of it fill the frame, collapses to slightly smaller than its final size, then gently breathes up to rest, as if the camera had found it.
techniques.use_when: The mark's first full appearance at the end, or a logo sting. A hit after a short bass gap. Marks with a strong silhouette or inner shapes that read as abstract fragments when huge.
techniques.avoid_when: Thin line marks (at macro scale they become two hairlines crossing the frame). Right after another zoom-through seam. The mark was already shown at hero size earlier (that makes this a replayed reveal).

techniques.name: Dark slam, spin and brighten
techniques.summary: After a near-still beat, giant low-contrast arms of the mark sweep over the frame, and the mark rushes back to logo size while spinning into place and brightening to full contrast.
techniques.use_when: The finale of a high-energy film, where the single biggest motion spike follows the single biggest stillness. Radially symmetric or rotational marks (asterisks, petals, rings).
techniques.avoid_when: Marks with an obvious up direction that look wrong at -70 deg (lettermarks). Calm films. Films that already used a spin or a fast zoom-out seam.

techniques.name: Seed build with stroke draw-on
techniques.summary: The mark grows from a small seed while its strokes, stripes or arcs draw on in a quick stagger, so it assembles itself in about half a second and the label rises in beside it.
techniques.use_when: Geometric marks made of a body plus lines, stripes or orbits. A fresh logo reveal after a hard cut to a clean stage. Stings that must show the mark within 0.5 s.
techniques.avoid_when: Solid single-shape marks (there is nothing to draw). Marks with more than ~5 parts (it turns into a slow queue). The mark already exists on screen as the story device.

techniques.name: Liquid blob resolves into the mark
techniques.summary: A dot, or two soft lobes sliding in from the sides, swells into a liquid blob that stretches, splits and snaps into the crisp geometric mark.
techniques.use_when: Products about raw input becoming structure, or about merging and joining. The story device is a dot. Marks made of a few separate primitives.
techniques.avoid_when: Marks with thin strokes or text inside (the threshold eats them). Brands that need crisp precision throughout. Films already using a soft morph seam.

techniques.name: Staircase echo shape morph
techniques.summary: A large brand shape collapses into a slim pill around the URL, and mid-morph its moving edges show stepped echoes from staggered copies, like a mechanical transformation.
techniques.use_when: Turning a big brand shape or frame into the CTA container. Mechanical, engineered or developer-tool brands. One moment that should feel designed rather than tweened.
techniques.avoid_when: Short moves (under ~150 px the echoes collapse into a smear). Elements that already carry motion blur (double trails). More than once per film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Draw the echoes as plain 1.5 px strokes in one tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.line on C.paper) with a linear opacity falloff. No rim light, bloom or coloured edges on the copies.

techniques.name: Story object becomes the mark
techniques.summary: The film's last object (a dot, circle, coin or pill) ends at exactly the mark's screen position and size, and the mark replaces it by a hard cut or an in-place morph, so the logo arrives as the answer to the story.
techniques.use_when: Every film that has a story device: the default way to arrive at the mark, especially as the device's third and final use.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no recurring object (a mark forced out of an unrelated shape reads as a pun). The object's shape and the mark's disagree (a square into a circle needs a morph, never a cut).

techniques.name: Words part, URL types into the gap
techniques.summary: The closing line splits at its middle, both halves slide outward and dim, the URL types letter by letter into the gap, and the flanks fade so the URL holds alone.
techniques.use_when: The closing line is a two-word phrase or pun built around the product, and the CTA is a URL. Minimal, type-only films.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines longer than ~4 words. Films with no typing anywhere else (it would add a new device at the very end). URLs too long for the gap to open within the safe width.

techniques.name: Card shrinks to a pill, words close in
techniques.summary: The last content card empties and shrinks into a small pill while the tagline words slide in from beyond the frame edges, blurred to sharp, to sit on either side of it; then the logo appears inside the pill.
techniques.use_when: Films that opened with a gap or pill inside a headline (the reverse closes the bookend). Products whose output is a card, post, message or result. A tagline that brackets the brand: [wordL] [mark] [wordR].
techniques.avoid_when: There is no card on screen to collapse. Words too long to fit beside the pill inside the safe width. Light-on-light stages where the pill loses its edge.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Make the pill opaque: a solid tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.mist on C.paper), optionally with a 1.5 px C.line stroke. No translucent fill and no backdrop blur over the background.

techniques.name: CTA line closes its gaps
techniques.summary: The end line starts with exaggerated spaces between its words, which close as the line settles centred; the last word, often the URL, travels farthest, so the eye ends there.
techniques.use_when: A one-line CTA (a sentence plus a URL) after a large type beat. Type-led films whose last beat is a phrase locking together.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines that wrap to two rows. Films that already closed a word gap earlier. Vertical frames where the stretched line would exceed the safe width.

techniques.name: The product clears the stage
techniques.summary: The last product element leaves (dropping out of frame, accelerating away, or bursting outward toward camera), and the brand, already waiting behind it, starts its reveal on the exact frame it is uncovered.
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs and feature films whose last shot is the product itself. The opening was a window or card entering, so the reverse bookends it. A crescendo of many screens that should give way to calm.
techniques.avoid_when: The film's last beat is type, not product. A lockup that is already visible would be crossed by the exiting product. A burst with no build-up earlier to justify the energy.

techniques.name: End card replays the opening
techniques.summary: The ending reuses the opening's stage and its mechanic, now carrying the brand, so the film closes on a rhyme the viewer has already learned.
techniques.use_when: Films with a distinctive opening mechanic or stage. The signature move's third use. Loops, where the end hands back to frame 0.
techniques.avoid_when: The opening was generic (replaying it only repeats a template). The reprise would be a frame-for-frame replay that adds nothing. Films under 10 s, where the rhyme has no time to land.

techniques.name: Lockup keeps building through the hold
techniques.summary: Once resolved, the lockup never freezes: the card slowly pushes in (or exhales back), the tracking tightens a touch and the stage dims, so the last 1.5-2 s read as intentional rather than stalled.
techniques.use_when: Every lockup and URL hold, and any card that must sit for more than 48 f.
techniques.avoid_when: A designed freeze of at most 15 f on a silence (then stop everything, the push included). Loops whose hold must end at the frame-0 scale (ease the push back down instead).

techniques.name: Stop-motion brand strobe
techniques.summary: A burst of hard-cut brand states (the poster, the lockup tiled in ever denser grids, one flood, the boxed wordmark, the glyph) flickers past in under a second as a punchy sign-off.
techniques.use_when: Social stings and launch films with a poster-driven or stop-motion identity. A re-energising coda after a quiet end card. Autoplay loops that need a clean reset point.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm or premium brands. Any film where you cannot keep large light-dark flips under 3 per second (photosensitivity). Any case where it would cut the lockup's hold below 1.5 s.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the cream flood with the film's single accent flood (or C.ink2), keep every other state on the dark stage, and allow only one bright state, so the strobe changes shape and density rather than luminance.

techniques.name: Accent icon cools to its neutral mark
techniques.summary: The app icon pops up from tiny in the film's hot accent, cools through darker tones to its neutral final colours, lifts a little to make room, and the name fades in beneath it.
techniques.use_when: Films whose accent stood for heat, urgency or the problem early on and should cool into the product. App-icon lockups.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent already means something else in the film (one accent, one meaning). Icons whose final colour is the accent itself.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Start the tile in the film's single accent as a flat fill, not a multi-hue gradient, and cool it through darker shades of that same hue to the neutral ink with mixColor. Any accent hue carries the idea, so it never needs a warm orange-to-red ramp.

techniques.name: Mark turns through a key light
techniques.summary: The mark (an extruded glyph, a coin or a tile) turns a few degrees in 3D, and its face passes through a light, so a single specular sweep crosses it as it settles face-on.
techniques.use_when: Premium, material or physical brands (finance, hardware, collectibles). 3D marks. A mark that needs one moment of life early in its hold.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat, playful or line marks (a sheen on a stroke looks like a template effect). Films with no other 3D. A second glint anywhere in the film (it reads as a preset).

techniques.name: Device keeps time inside the lockup
techniques.summary: During the hold, the story device that became part of the mark (a dot, a bar, a stripe) gives one or two small ticks on the beat, so the bookend plays inside the finished lockup instead of after it.
techniques.use_when: Films whose story device became a piece of the mark. Ends that should close the device's loop without ending on the device alone.
techniques.avoid_when: Marks without a separable piece. Very still closes, where any pulse breaks the calm. Loops that need the device to travel back to its frame-0 position instead.

techniques.name: Monochrome world, one accent
techniques.summary: Everything is black, white and grey, and one saturated accent marks the single element in each shot that carries the meaning.
techniques.use_when: Films that mix photos, 3D, maps and UI, multi-cell layouts, or any shot where several things compete and the eye needs exactly one target.
techniques.avoid_when: The product's own colourful UI is the subject of every shot and greying it would misrepresent it, or the story needs two semantic colours on screen at once.

techniques.name: One-hue light ramp
techniques.summary: Every lit thing (rims, rings, stage lifts, the end-card field) comes from adjacent lightness steps of one hue on a single near-black stage.
techniques.use_when: Dark launch films with many light-built shapes (orbs, rings, rims) that need a recognisable look. It also makes a single bright card hit harder.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode walkthroughs where the UI's own colours dominate, or films already using the monochrome-plus-accent system (pick one system).

techniques.name: Accent ground for claims only
techniques.summary: Narrative shots sit on the neutral stage, other claims flip to the opposite neutral, and the single full-bleed accent ground is saved for the hero claim or the closing card, so colour works as punctuation.
techniques.use_when: Films with a few big statements that must feel louder than the walkthrough around them, and endings that need to feel conclusive.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent fails contrast as a ground for display type, or the film has no distinct claims (a pure UI tour).

techniques.name: Single inversion card
techniques.summary: In an otherwise dark film, one card cuts to a near-white field with dark type for one second, marking the key promise.
techniques.use_when: A dark film's single most important promise needs to stop the viewer halfway through.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode films, films that already alternate dark and light, or when the music has no gap to place it in.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep a neutral C.paper field, never a cream one. Draw the ring as a single hard-edged accent stroke (a 6-10 px ellipse at 88% of the frame) that breathes in scale, with no soft colour falloff and no second hue.

techniques.name: Theme flip mid-move
techniques.summary: In the middle of a camera fly-over, the dark page and stage flash to their light versions, top first, and the motion never pauses.
techniques.use_when: Products with dark and light modes, or as the single dark-to-light act transition of a film.
techniques.avoid_when: The camera is static (the flip turns into a plain crossfade), or the light version would not match the dark one pixel for pixel.

techniques.name: Palette shift as context cue
techniques.summary: The world's colour changes behind a steady foreground, for a whole act or for one beat, to say 'new context' or 'this is the moment' without words.
techniques.use_when: Act changes without title cards, entering another app's world, or flagging the key moment (the user's prompt, the reveal).
techniques.avoid_when: The foreground is moving at the same time (the cue gets lost), or the film is shorter than two acts.

techniques.name: Ink resolve on arrival
techniques.summary: Text never simply fades in: it arrives pale (or dim on a dark stage) and darkens or brightens to full ink as it settles.
techniques.use_when: Every headline and caption reveal, especially over textured or busy backgrounds where an opacity fade alone looks washed out.
techniques.avoid_when: Numbers that must read instantly on a cut (land them at full ink), or type that already sits inside a colour-band fill.

techniques.name: Accent on the newest arrival
techniques.summary: Whatever just arrived (a typed character, a snapped word, a generated pill) wears the accent for a moment and then settles to neutral, so a short coloured wake leads the eye.
techniques.use_when: Prompts typing, statements building word by word, AI-generated items appearing, or any build where the newest piece should lead.
techniques.avoid_when: The accent already means something else in the shot (a focus ring or a pressed button), or long paragraphs where the wake becomes noise.

techniques.name: Accent hit envelope
techniques.summary: On a press or an impact, the element floods with the accent and peaks for one frame with its label inverted, then either bleeds back like decaying light or stays as the new state.
techniques.use_when: Primary-button clicks, send or confirm moments, and contact hits that turn an object into its new state.
techniques.avoid_when: Secondary controls and hovers (save it for the decisive action), or when the accent already floods the ground.

techniques.name: Specular sweep
techniques.summary: A soft bright band glides once across a settled number, word or logo face, so the element looks locked and made of a real material without moving.
techniques.use_when: A final number, price or logo that has landed and must hold attention through a still beat, or loading and generating labels.
techniques.avoid_when: The element is still moving, or you would need more than one sweep in the shot (it turns into decoration).

techniques.name: Rim streak on card edges
techniques.summary: A bright streak travels along a dark card's border while its edges carry a faint lit rim, separating it from a black stage without a drop shadow.
techniques.use_when: Flat dark UI cards floating on pure black that need depth and separation without tilting or shadows.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode UI (use a soft neutral shadow instead), or several cards on screen at once (the streaks compete).
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Drop the coloured halos entirely. Use one 1 px single-colour border highlight sweeping along the edge, plus a neutral low-opacity drop shadow (0 24px 48px of C.ink at 50%) for lift.

techniques.name: Travelling tone band fill
techniques.summary: A word, URL or logo mark fills through a band of colour (dark, then accent, then light) that sweeps across it and settles on the final ink.
techniques.use_when: Hero words, the URL card, or a logo mark that should introduce the accent before it fills the frame.
techniques.avoid_when: Small UI text, or type that is still moving (the band and the motion fight).

techniques.name: Living gradient stage
techniques.summary: Behind static cards the background never freezes: soft pools of colour at the corners breathe in brightness or drift slowly, like light through water.
techniques.use_when: Holds, end cards and statement cards that would otherwise sit still for more than 48 f.
techniques.avoid_when: Busy UI shots where any background motion competes, or films built on a hard flat-stage look. Behind a product window or readable type, where soft pools read as a generic gradient backdrop or as haze; light stages, where they read as smudges. A flat stage with one tonal step is the stronger default.

techniques.name: Light swell bridge into the hero
techniques.summary: Light swells around a small panel until the frame is bright, the film cuts on the brightest frame to the hero card sitting in the same light, and that light slowly exhales back to dark.
techniques.use_when: Releasing a dark section into the hero card or title: the biggest reveal in a dark film.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode films, or a second time in the same film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the soft multi-hue bloom with four hard-edged concentric discs in tonal steps of one hue (the stage, then 15%, 35% and 60% lightness toward the accent), their radii expanding with a 2 f stagger on normal blend. Keep the same swell, cut and exhale timing.

techniques.name: Rising colour wash carrier
techniques.summary: A soft single-hue field rises from the bottom edge behind the type, swells and sweeps up across the frame on the change, then recedes off the top, so the foreground swap reads as one move.
techniques.use_when: Changing cards behind continuous colour, leading into an accent-ground claim or the end card, or smoothing a hard cut into a new scene.
techniques.avoid_when: Shots already on an accent ground, or dense UI that the wash would tint. A soft accent haze behind type reads as glow.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep the move and lose the soft falloff: a flat accent band with a crisp, straight top edge (a clip-path inset driven by the same Y curve) rises behind the type, sweeps up across the frame on the change and leaves off the top, at full opacity in a light tint of the accent. The swap still happens on its fastest frame; no radial gradient, no feathered edge.

techniques.name: Drain the stage, keep the hero
techniques.summary: Everything around the hero fades and the world drops to dark or bleaches to white, while the hero stays crisp in place, isolating it or closing a section.
techniques.use_when: Search results, a found item, a selected post or row, the moment before a detail view, and the ends of sections or of the film.
techniques.avoid_when: The hero itself must move during the isolation, or the neighbours carry context the viewer still needs.

techniques.name: Tilt-linked sheen
techniques.summary: As a card or device tilts in 3D, a faint highlight band slides across its face in step with the angle, so the surface reads as a real material catching a key light.
techniques.use_when: Perspective UI tilt-ups, cards flipping or settling out of 3D, device turns, and logo tiles yawing.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat 2D layouts with no rotation (use the one-shot specular sweep instead).

techniques.name: Duotone until featured
techniques.summary: Screenshots and photos sit in a two-tone grade until their beat. Then full colour opens out from the point of interaction, and the previous item returns to duotone.
techniques.use_when: Grids of integrations, galleries, template pickers, and multi-cell layouts where one item at a time is the subject.
techniques.avoid_when: Only one hero screenshot is on screen (nothing to contrast with), or the UI's colours are its selling point in every frame.

techniques.name: Key-light edge hairline
techniques.summary: Every card, device bezel and bevelled shape on a dark stage carries a hairline edge that is bright on the side facing one fixed key light and fades to nothing on the far side, so surfaces separate from black without shadows or halos.
techniques.use_when: Dark UI films with flat cards, panels, device bezels or bevelled brand shapes on near-black, where a drop shadow disappears and a glow is off-limits.
techniques.avoid_when: Light-mode shots, where a white hairline vanishes on paper. Also avoid it on cards that already carry cl-rim-light-sweep's travelling streak, and on layouts so dense that every lit edge turns the frame into wireframe noise.

techniques.name: Brightness rides the move
techniques.summary: A mark or icon takes its brightness from the same progress that drives its scale or depth, so an oversized pass stays a dark shape and the object reaches full brightness exactly as it lands.
techniques.use_when: A logo mark or icon slams in oversized and shrinks to size, an icon lifts out of the UI toward camera, or a field of objects at several depths is pushed through on a dark stage.
techniques.avoid_when: Text (use cl-ink-resolve, which runs on time), and moves under about 150 px or 1.5x, where the change would not show. On a light stage a giant near-black pass would itself be the flash, so mix toward the paper there.

techniques.name: Now, was, next tone ladder
techniques.summary: Items in a sequence sit on three neutral tones: the one being read is at full ink, the ones already read step down to a mid grey and stay as context, and the ones still to come wait in a dim grey.
techniques.use_when: Captions that build in steps, lists and checklists that grow, slot rollers, status sequences, and flanking words that make way for a new focal word.
techniques.avoid_when: A single statement that lands all at once, or real product UI whose own text colours must stay true. In lens lists, tone should follow distance from the focus line, not reading order.

techniques.name: Graphic softens into the stage
techniques.summary: A crisp graphic that has just finished its move, such as a wall of bars or a stripe field, loses its edges, widens and keeps drifting until it has become the soft backdrop for the next title, with no cut.
techniques.use_when: After a graphic build (a bar wall, a stripe or tile field, a filled pattern), when the next beat is a title or the end-card mark and needs a backdrop born from what was just on screen.
techniques.avoid_when: The graphic carries data the viewer still needs to read, or it is a UI act where the stage should stay flat. When no graphic build comes before the title, use cl-living-stage directly.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Fill the bars with tonal steps of one non-banned hue (from the stage to a light tint), not a periwinkle-pink-orange spectrum, so the softened field becomes a single-hue living stage. Keep the RackFocus soften, the widen and the per-bar drift.

techniques.name: Rolling band flood
techniques.summary: A light frame fills with the brand colour as soft horizontal bands of it roll upward and grow opaque. The text tints and dissolves into it, and the film arrives on its end-card field without a cut.
techniques.use_when: Closing a light product act into the end card, or returning to the brand world after the last UI beat (a success state, a published page) without a hard cut.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark films, where the flood reads as fog over black. Also avoid it a second time in the same film, and before an end card whose ground is not the flood's hue.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Build the bands only from tonal steps of one non-banned hue (light tint, mid tint, the accent), not a lavender-pink-peach-orange spectrum. Keep the roll, the p^2 opacity ramp and the text absorption.

techniques.name: Shadows tinted by the stage
techniques.summary: On a tinted light stage, lifted cards and solid pills cast soft shadows in a dark step of the stage's own hue instead of grey, so depth reads as part of the world's colour rather than dirt on it.
techniques.use_when: Light-mode acts on pale tinted stages, pastel product worlds, and black pills or tiles floating on a tinted field where a grey shadow looks muddy.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark stages, where a coloured shadow becomes a glow. Keep shadows neutral in neutral C.paper films, and skip the tint wherever it would echo the accent and spend its meaning.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Use only one dark step of the stage's own hue, on light stages only, with shadows that fall downward and never spread past about half the element's size. On dark stages, drop the tint entirely and separate cards with cl-key-light-edge-hairline instead of a coloured halo.

techniques.name: Type solidity arc
techniques.summary: The type gains body across the film. Early statements are translucent white that lets the coloured stage show through, and the closing line and lockup are solid, so the payoff reads as more certain than the promise.
techniques.use_when: Brand films and launches on a coloured or living stage, built as question to answer or promise to proof, where the closing line should feel firmer than the opening.
techniques.avoid_when: Neutral black or grey stages, where translucent white just reads as dim grey. Also avoid it for small UI text, in films under about 10 s, and on light stages, where translucent ink loses contrast.

techniques.name: Speed-gated motion blur
techniques.summary: Fast whips, flings and flicked scrolls streak like a real shutter while holds and slow drifts stay pin-sharp, so the eye rests on the readable frames.
techniques.use_when: Any film with whips, flings, drops or flicked scrolls; walkthroughs that travel fast between setups and need every hold razor-sharp.
techniques.avoid_when: Moves that would need more than 80 px/f (redesign as a cut on the beat, a match cut or a mask wipe); readable text moving above 20 px/f; a deliberately stepped on-twos section.

techniques.name: Stepped cadence on twos
techniques.summary: One designated layer or section updates only on every second frame, so its motion reads crisp, precise and slightly mechanical against an otherwise smooth 60 fps film.
techniques.use_when: Mechanical, developer or precision brands; a UI section that should feel like a live screen; a short sting that wants a punchy graphic cadence.
techniques.avoid_when: Slow drifts and camera pushes (they judder); moves that would exceed 24 px per step; a few isolated shots in a smooth film, where it reads as dropped frames.

techniques.name: One grade across mixed media
techniques.summary: Desaturated photography, matte grey 3D, flat vector maps and line diagrams cut freely against each other without clashing, because every medium shares one dark value range and only the hero prop carries the accent.
techniques.use_when: Films that must combine photos, renders, maps, diagrams and UI, especially grid or bento layouts with several media on screen at once.
techniques.avoid_when: Light, pastel or colourful brands; single-medium films; hero product photography that must keep its true colour.

techniques.name: Low-luma photo plate
techniques.summary: A real photograph sits behind the UI or type, graded almost to black or thrown out of focus, adding context and tonal texture without stealing contrast from the copy.
techniques.use_when: Dark-stage films that need real-world context (a desk, a city, a workspace) or a material, crafted feel behind sparse type or a floating panel.
techniques.avoid_when: Light stages; a busy photo that stays above ~12% mean luma and fights the type; stock imagery unrelated to the product's world; decorative bokeh that names no job.

techniques.name: Global frame-keyed grain
techniques.summary: A fine, even grain sits over the whole film at one strength, breaking banding in soft ramps and blurred plates and giving flat colour fields a tactile surface.
techniques.use_when: Films with large flat or saturated colour fields, soft lighting ramps, blurred photo plates, or a tactile, filmic brand.
techniques.avoid_when: Crisp, clinical UI films where any texture reads as dirt; when the strength would have to change between scenes; as a fix for banding that dithered PNGs should solve.

techniques.name: Stipple only in lit ramps
techniques.summary: A visible dithered stipple lives only inside lit edges and light falloffs, while the flat stage around them stays perfectly clean.
techniques.use_when: Dark films with lit edges, light pools or soft falloffs that risk banding, where a global grain would dirty a deliberately clean stage.
techniques.avoid_when: Films already running global grain (double texture); light stages; hard-edged flat design with no ramps.

techniques.name: Faint dot-matrix silhouette
techniques.summary: Behind a claim, a barely visible field of dots forms a meaningful silhouette (a world map, a region, the product's own shape), adding literal context without competing with the type.
techniques.use_when: Claims about reach, coverage, location or scale, and any shot where a silhouette adds literal meaning behind the copy.
techniques.avoid_when: Generic decoration with no meaning; contrast above ~6%, where it starts competing with the copy; small vertical frames where 13 px dots read as noise (scale the pitch up instead).

techniques.name: Scanline transmutation
techniques.summary: A bright bar sweeps down a hero object: above the bar the object has already become its digital form, a dot-matrix disc with a crisp rim, while below it the original solid object remains.
techniques.use_when: One hero transformation per film: an object becoming its private, digital, encrypted or connected form; the moment the concept turns.
techniques.avoid_when: More than once per film; ordinary UI state changes; objects under ~25% of frame height, where the dot pitch cannot read.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep the sweep but drop the bloom and the tint: a flat, hard-edged bar 12-24 px thick in white or the accent (or a 2 px hairline with a 10% tint band 40 px behind it), dots in white or the accent, never violet, and nothing lit outside the object's outline.

techniques.name: Locked-state mosaic
techniques.summary: Withheld content shows as pixelated, desaturated, darkened art with a lock glyph and thin light lines sliding across it, until an unlock snaps it to clean full-tone art.
techniques.use_when: Premium, gated or upcoming features; a reveal sequence where concealment builds desire; access or unlock stories.
techniques.avoid_when: Products with nothing gated; text content (pixelated text reads as broken); more than one reveal device in the same act.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the soft, screen-blended gaussian light ribbons with crisp 1.5-2 px strokes at 30-60% white, and keep the unlock's brightness overshoot inside the card: no burst or rays past its edge.

techniques.name: Intersecting ring field
techniques.summary: Above and below a centred band of type, families of huge overlapping ellipse outlines rotate slowly in opposite directions and whip on every copy swap, giving the words an ownable abstract environment.
techniques.use_when: Type-led launch cards or a statement sequence on a dark stage that needs a signature environment and a motivated way to change copy without cuts.
techniques.avoid_when: UI demos, where it competes with the product; light stages, where 2 px rings vanish; more than ~4 s of pure ambience.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Drop the soft-lit two-hue gradient strokes, the inner blur and the screen blend: every ring is a crisp 2 px stroke in one neutral (white at 15-60% on ink), normal blend, with depth carried by per-ring opacity alone. Keep the rings out of the accent so the accent keeps its one meaning.

techniques.name: Brushed micro-streaks
techniques.summary: Fine directional streaks and a satin grain across a hero object's face make it read as machined material instead of flat vector.
techniques.use_when: Hero objects shown big enough for micro detail (coins, cards, devices, extruded marks); hardware and finance brands with a physical metaphor.
techniques.avoid_when: Small or minified objects, where 1 px streaks alias and crawl; soft, friendly brands; flat UI.

techniques.name: Glyph-grid shock pulse
techniques.summary: On the film's biggest hit, the dark background flashes a grid of tiny monoline marks that bend outward from the impact like a shockwave, then settles back to a quiet grained field.
techniques.use_when: A digital or developer brand's payoff hit or lockup landing that needs a shockwave without colour or glow.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films; more than once per film; light stages; behind type that is still arriving.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Keep it strictly grid-locked so it reads as structure, not a burst: plus marks only, every cell on the grid with no scatter or random drift, opacity capped at 0.35, a single displacement ring, monochrome, and no streaks of light.

techniques.name: Gobo-lit studio backdrop
techniques.summary: The UI floats over an off-white studio backdrop crossed by huge, very soft diagonal shadows, like window light through leaves, so flat screens feel photographed.
techniques.use_when: Light-stage product films and walkthroughs that need depth and physicality without glass, colour or a 3D set.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark stages; dense UI that fills the frame edge to edge; strictly flat graphic brands.

techniques.name: Fog floor
techniques.summary: The bottom fifth of the frame lightens toward the stage's brightest tone, as if the UI hovers above a softly lit floor that receding planes can sink into.
techniques.use_when: Light or pastel stages with 3D tilt-backs, lifts and recedes; any film that wants a horizon without drawing a floor.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat, front-on UI with no depth moves; dark stages that already have a light pool; vertical frames where captions sit in the bottom fifth.

techniques.name: Micro-tick UI sound
techniques.summary: (Sound) Typing and UI changes get tiny, dry ticks at or under the music, and once the drums run the UI goes silent, so the picture feels tactile without a loud keyboard sample.
techniques.use_when: Typed prompts, word-by-word builds, cold opens before the beat drops, any UI moment that wants touch without an effect announcing itself.
techniques.avoid_when: Under voiceover syllables; inside a dense drum section; loud keyboard samples; a film whose idea is silent UI over a beat bed throughout.

techniques.name: Hairline edge and key shadow
techniques.summary: Every floating surface gets a 1 px edge plus one soft key shadow on paper, or a top inner highlight on ink, so flat UI reads as a physical object in a lit space.
techniques.use_when: Any floating card, panel, modal or window, in every format.
techniques.avoid_when: Flush full-bleed UI or gutterless grids whose cells should merge into one canvas; anything tempting a glass panel or a coloured halo instead.

techniques.name: Feathered edge mask
techniques.summary: Lists, reels and overflowing lines dissolve into the stage at a soft edge instead of being cut by a hard crop, so content feels endless and the eye stays in the clear middle.
techniques.use_when: Endless-feeling lists, proof reels, logs, chats, card stacks, and type that overflows its line as it is typed.
techniques.avoid_when: Content that must be read right at the container edge; a hard-cropped bento look; as a full-frame vignette (that is lighting, not a mask).

techniques.name: Stepped mosaic resolve
techniques.summary: An image or screen arrives as coarse grey blocks that halve in size every two frames until the real picture snaps in, sharp and in full colour.
techniques.use_when: Revealing an image, avatar, map or screen in a digital or tech brand; the resolve after a locked state; a beat-synced reveal.
techniques.avoid_when: Text-heavy screens (half-resolved text looks broken); calm, quiet brands; more than twice per film.

techniques.name: Wireframe-to-product scan
techniques.summary: A thin accent line sweeps across a UI card: ahead of it the card is still a wireframe of outlines and skeleton bars, behind it the finished product is already there.
techniques.use_when: Idea-to-product, design-to-code, generation or build stories; the first appearance of the hero UI.
techniques.avoid_when: More than once per film; UI too sparse to read as a wireframe; a film that already uses another scan device such as scanline transmutation.

techniques.name: Halftone shading
techniques.summary: A flat hero shape gains volume from a single-colour halftone dot field whose dots swell in the shadow side and shrink toward a slowly moving light.
techniques.use_when: Flat marks, icons or objects that need volume without 3D; technical or print-minded brands; alongside other dot-matrix devices.
techniques.avoid_when: Shapes under ~200 px, where the dots turn to mush; photographic or 3D scenes; busy UI behind the shape.

techniques.name: Swarm, cluster and burst reveal
techniques.summary: About twenty cards or screenshots fly in from every edge, swirl, pack into a dense overlapping cluster that slowly swells, then blow outward past the camera to uncover a hero object that was waiting behind them.
techniques.use_when: A crescendo near the end that proves breadth (many apps, templates, outputs) and clears the stage for the lockup or a hero stat; the film's single biggest motion spike.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm or minimal films, more than once per film, or when the cards' content has to be read (nothing in the swarm is legible). If it reveals the lockup, the lockup still holds only 1.5-2.0 s.

techniques.name: Arc carousel
techniques.summary: A row of cards rides a wide smile-shaped arc across the lower part of the frame, each tilted tangent to the curve, rushing in, coasting slowly through the middle and speeding out.
techniques.use_when: Showing an inventory or collection (templates, cards, products, integrations) where several items should read at once and the set should feel endless; a looping feature beat.
techniques.avoid_when: Items with dense text that must be read at the edges (tilted edge cards are glanced at, not read), or vertical frames where the arc gets too tight.

techniques.name: Hero icon becomes the inline glyph
techniques.summary: The centred hero icon shrinks and travels into a slot at the start of, or inside, a sentence, and the words of the claim spill out of it, so the icon becomes a word.
techniques.use_when: Bridging from a hero object to a claim about it: an icon becoming the bullet of its benefit, a mark becoming the subject of a sentence, a feature glyph leading a metric line.
techniques.avoid_when: Detailed icons that will not read at cap height (50-90 px), or sentences long enough to wrap.

techniques.name: Headline over a ghost of the UI
techniques.summary: A headline inks in from light grey to near-black while a faint copy of the product interface sits behind it, then the UI resolves to full strength as the headline leaves.
techniques.use_when: Setting up a demo during a statement, so the move into the product needs no transition; a claim that names the product area about to be shown.
techniques.avoid_when: High-contrast UIs whose ghost would muddy the type, or UI text at the same scale as the headline sitting directly behind it.

techniques.name: Icon-led ragged word stack
techniques.summary: A short lead word is followed by three or four keywords on separate lines, each with a small line icon, set at staggered x positions so the list has a rag instead of bullets.
techniques.use_when: Listing three or four abstract capabilities, platforms or audiences that would otherwise be a bullet list; a 'works across X, Y, Z' beat.
techniques.avoid_when: More than four items, items longer than two words, or icons that decorate rather than mean something (then drop them and keep the rag).
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Drop the muted lead word above the stack: fold it into the first row as a full-strength word at the keywords' size ('Built for teams', then 'agencies' and 'founders' on the rag), or cut it and let the keywords stand alone. Use an icon only where it is the product's own mark for that item, never a stock line icon; otherwise keep the rag with words alone. Keep the rag table, the 10 f row stagger and the 0.4 px/f drift.

techniques.name: Hub-and-spoke concept diagram
techniques.summary: A central product tile sits inside two thin concentric rings with a short streak orbiting it, inputs on the left and outputs on the right, under a centred one-line headline.
techniques.use_when: Explaining a many-inputs, many-outputs product (integrations, sources to results) in one still composition without narration; the concept beat before a walkthrough.
techniques.avoid_when: More than five chips per side, or when the real product UI can show the same thing directly.

techniques.name: Mark set as a word
techniques.summary: A logo, partner mark or icon sits inside a sentence on the baseline at cap height, as if it were a word, appearing with its own delayed fade or swapping with a word in the same slot.
techniques.use_when: Co-branding inside a claim, naming a platform or integration without a separate logo slate, or turning a generic noun into the product name in place.
techniques.avoid_when: Marks with fine detail or wide aspect ratios that cannot read at cap height, or the film's own final lockup, which appears once, at the end, on its own.

techniques.name: Caption in the subject's negative space
techniques.summary: Each camera move ends on a pose where the product covers about two-thirds of the frame and leaves a clean band of empty stage, and the caption builds inside that band.
techniques.use_when: Single-take product walkthroughs and 3D UI slabs where each feature gets one pose and one caption; any shot where text laid over the UI would fight it.
techniques.avoid_when: The subject must stay full-frame to be legible (caption above or below it instead), or a 9:16 frame, where the band should be top or bottom only.

techniques.name: Opposite-corner caption relay
techniques.summary: One caption fades out of one upper corner while the next starts building in the mirrored corner, so the eye travels across a locked frame and that travel is the motion.
techniques.use_when: Two consecutive beats over one held product shot with no camera move or cut; alternating claims about one screen.
techniques.avoid_when: Captions longer than a short line (the eye cannot finish A while B starts), or as the default for every caption change; repeated more than twice it reads as a device.

techniques.name: One huge centred subject
techniques.summary: Every frame has exactly one subject, centred and large: a single line of type, or one UI card scaled to most of the frame width and often bleeding past the edges, with everything else dimmed.
techniques.use_when: Fast, phone-first films; walkthroughs where the viewer must never search for the subject; the default framing between more designed compositions.
techniques.avoid_when: Comparison or cause-and-effect beats that need two things on screen at once (use a split), or bento-style loops.

techniques.name: Centre object with mirrored flanks
techniques.summary: A narrow centre object (a phone-width window, a pill, a big number) holds the middle while matching elements sit on both sides: the two halves of a caption, or two mirrored columns of items.
techniques.use_when: A narrow device or pill leaves empty sides; a stat that needs visible volume on either side; inputs and outputs around one product; the tagline that frames a logo pill before the end.
techniques.avoid_when: Wide centre subjects (each flank gets squeezed under 20% of the frame), or vertical formats (stack above and below instead).

techniques.name: Subtract to the one
techniques.summary: A busy board loses its elements one by one until a single survivor remains, which either re-centres or stays exactly where it was while the world around it dims.
techniques.use_when: Isolating the deliverable, the found result or the keyword before entering its world; turning a crowded problem state into one focus.
techniques.avoid_when: The removed elements are themselves the message (show them first), or the survivor is small enough to float lost in an empty frame (push in after isolating it).

techniques.name: Words part for an inserted object
techniques.summary: Inside a finished line, the words slide apart to open a gap and an object pops into it (an icon, a photo, a token, or a caret that grows into a container), so the sentence becomes a frame for the object.
techniques.use_when: Making a sentence about the object literally contain it (a product photo in a claim, a lock icon beside 'private', a prompt box between two words); morphing a headline into the first UI element of the next scene.
techniques.avoid_when: Long lines whose parted words would leave the frame unintentionally, or an object that needs more room than a word gap can give (use a push-aside or a cut).

techniques.name: Live cause-and-effect split
techniques.summary: Two panels share the frame side by side, the cause on one side (a chat, a list, an input) and the effect on the other (a generated page, a photo, a result), both live, while the camera creeps in.
techniques.use_when: Showing that an input produces an output (prompt to page, list to detail, setting to preview), where seeing both at once is the point.
techniques.avoid_when: Phone-first or vertical films (stack the two instead), or when either side's text would drop under 24 px at 1080p.

techniques.name: Bento cell takes over the frame
techniques.summary: In a flush four-cell grid, one cell grows to fill the whole frame while its siblings are pushed off the edges, still playing as they go, turning a breadth overview into one focused shot without a cut.
techniques.use_when: A loop or launch that opens on four-up breadth and then dives into one feature; returning to the overview between features.
techniques.avoid_when: A chosen cell whose scene was not composed for full frame (it will look sparse), or more than twice per film.

techniques.name: Vertical clear-band stack
techniques.summary: In a 9:16 frame, the caption and the subject stack vertically inside the band the feed leaves clear, with their combined mass centred on that band rather than on the frame, and nothing important under the bottom caption zone or the right action rail.
techniques.use_when: Any vertical cut-down or vertical-first film for feeds.
techniques.avoid_when: 16:9 masters (use a side-by-side composition there), or full-bleed moments where one giant word fills the screen anyway.

techniques.name: Breath envelope per card
techniques.summary: Every card arrives fast and decelerates, keeps moving gently through its hold, then accelerates away and is cut on its fastest frame.
techniques.use_when: Statement cards, kinetic type and feature cards in a fast-cut film where nothing should ever look frozen.
techniques.avoid_when: Dense UI that needs a dead-still read (lock the camera instead), and the final lockup hold.

techniques.name: Camera locks, the interface performs
techniques.summary: After each move the camera stops dead, and for a 1-4 s read only the caption, the cursor and one micro-interaction move.
techniques.use_when: Dense product UI that must be read, walkthroughs, and films where every move should feel deliberate because it contrasts with stillness.
techniques.avoid_when: Kinetic type or fast montages where a dead camera reads as a stalled player, or holds with nothing in the UI to animate.

techniques.name: The one long hold
techniques.summary: In a film that otherwise never stops, a single key claim sits nearly still for over a second, which tells the viewer it is the line to remember.
techniques.use_when: The single claim or number the film exists to say, in a launch film or short spot that is relentless everywhere else.
techniques.avoid_when: Films already built on long holds, where it stops reading as special, or when two lines compete for the slot.

techniques.name: Hard stop into a silent sign-off
techniques.summary: Tension rises under the back half, the music stops dead on the cut to the last line or URL, the picture all but freezes, and the lockup arrives at full speed under a single low stinger.
techniques.use_when: The last 4-6 s of launch films and feature reels for fast, confident brands.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm brands, where a sub stinger reads as trailer noise (end on one soft chord instead), and loops with no ending.

techniques.name: Spectacle, diagram, walkthrough, sign-off
techniques.summary: A launch film in four sequences: a short spectacle open, one concept diagram, a long real-product walkthrough and a brief brand close.
techniques.use_when: 30-60 s launch films that have to earn attention, explain an idea and then prove it in the product.
techniques.avoid_when: Spots under 15 s (use the image-then-type plan instead) and products with nothing to diagram.

techniques.name: Image act, then type act
techniques.summary: A short spot splits in half: the first half is pure imagery with no words at all, the second is pure type with no imagery.
techniques.use_when: 6-12 s spots and social cut-downs with one claim and a strong visual metaphor, especially when watched on mute.
techniques.avoid_when: Product walkthroughs that need captions on the UI, and films over 20 s.

techniques.name: Light and dark as chapters
techniques.summary: Acts are planned by stage polarity, dark for the abstract or problem beats and light for the product, so chapter changes read without any title cards.
techniques.use_when: Films with distinct problem/solution or prompt/result halves, and 20-60 s pieces that need a rhythm at the scale of whole acts.
techniques.avoid_when: Very short stings, and brands locked to a single stage colour.

techniques.name: Oner through a morph chain
techniques.summary: The whole film plays as one continuous shot, every new scene growing out of an object already on screen, with no hard cuts at all.
techniques.use_when: Multi-step workflows and multi-app stories, or any film where the viewer should never have to re-orient.
techniques.avoid_when: Films that use polarity cuts as punctuation, or footage-based shots that cannot share elements.

techniques.name: One camera journey across one surface
techniques.summary: Every product state lives on one large surface and the film is a single camera path between poses; scene changes are pushes, pulls, orbits, whips and the interface's own window actions.
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs of a single app, features where spatial orientation matters, and calm, premium product films.
techniques.avoid_when: Multi-app or abstract stories, and films under 10 s.

techniques.name: Travelling thread object
techniques.summary: One small accent object (a dot, a packet or a streak) recurs across shots and acts, carrying the idea from problem to feature to feature as a single causal chain.
techniques.use_when: Abstract or concept-led launch films whose beats are visually disconnected, and stories about value or data travelling.
techniques.avoid_when: Plain UI walkthroughs where a cursor already guides the eye, since two guides compete.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Same Thread component in the single brand accent: an opaque head with a solid tapered tail and no halo or bloom, and the same hue on every beat. Impacts read through squash() and a hitPulse scale bump on the struck element rather than a flash of light.

techniques.name: Each repeat runs faster
techniques.summary: The first instance of a repeated action plays at full length, the second runs about 40% quicker, and later ones are implied or ratchet faster still.
techniques.use_when: Repeated unlocks, card reveals, list items, word deletes, and captions that recur across a film.
techniques.avoid_when: Items that each need a full read, and the first instance, which must teach the pattern at full length.

techniques.name: Fixed-length ask, variable answer
techniques.summary: A demo repeats a fixed-length ask beat followed by a result whose length varies with its importance, so the rhythm teaches itself and the variations prevent fatigue.
techniques.use_when: Prompt-to-result products, feature tours with one repeated action, and walkthroughs of 3-6 capabilities.
techniques.avoid_when: Fewer than 3 instances (there is no pattern to learn), and stings.

techniques.name: Phrase chunks on the beat
techniques.summary: A line arrives in two or three chunks split by meaning, each landing exactly on the next beat, so the reading rhythm is performed by the track.
techniques.use_when: Statement lines over music with a clear pulse, launch openers, and 3-7 word claims.
techniques.avoid_when: No music or a free-time score, and sentences of more than 8 words.

techniques.name: Empty ground after a cut
techniques.summary: Right after some hard cuts the new stage shows for two empty frames before its type appears, a tiny palate cleanser that makes the cut read crisply without any flash.
techniques.use_when: Type-led films on white or flat stages with many statement cuts.
techniques.avoid_when: Velocity-matched cuts, where the gap kills the momentum, and frame 0.

techniques.name: Music hole, then slam on the cut
techniques.summary: The low end, or the whole bed, vanishes for a fraction of a second under a key statement, then slams back on the exact frame of a picture event.
techniques.use_when: Statement cards, key claims and the hero cut in any film with a groove bed.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm brands with no drums, or more than one hole every 8 bars, where it stops working as an accent.

techniques.name: Score arranged to the acts
techniques.summary: The music's arrangement tells the story's structure: a sparse filtered intro, the drop on the first product frame, a breakdown for the calm act, a return for the proof, a final hit on the climax and the logo in silence.
techniques.use_when: 20-60 s launch films with clear acts, when the score is generated or its stems can be edited.
techniques.avoid_when: A supplied track with a fixed structure (retime the picture to its bars instead), and 3-6 s stings.

techniques.name: Silent UI over a steady bed
techniques.summary: In dense, fast-changing sequences the interface makes no sound of its own, with no per-key or per-event effects, and a steady groove carries all the energy.
techniques.use_when: Loops, grids, speed-typed prompts, counters, and any sequence with more than 3 events per second.
techniques.avoid_when: Sparse, calm films where each event deserves its own tuned sound, and the payoff moment.

techniques.name: Accelerando into the climax
techniques.summary: Shot lengths shrink step by step toward the climax, then one designed freeze on silence resets the clock just before the payoff lands.
techniques.use_when: The run-up to a reveal, a collage burst or the lockup in launch films and stings.
techniques.avoid_when: Walkthroughs where each shot carries UI that must be read, and films already cutting under 60 f per shot throughout.

techniques.name: Loop seam hidden at a motion peak
techniques.summary: A loop wraps around on the fastest frame of a whip or push, so the last frame flows into the first with no visible restart.
techniques.use_when: Autoplay loops for social, landing pages and product pages.
techniques.avoid_when: Pieces that end on a lockup (it appears once, at the end), and loops whose first frame must work as a readable poster.

techniques.name: Silence as the default bed
techniques.summary: There is no running music: most of the film is true silence, sound appears only on decisive events, one low swell carries the single reveal act, and the audio cuts dead on the frame a key value lands.
techniques.use_when: Short stings and feature spots under about 15 s, calm or premium tones, number and unlock reveals, and films with fewer than about one decisive event per second.
techniques.avoid_when: Launch films and walkthroughs over about 20 s, dense sequences with more than about 3 visible events per second (use a steady bed instead), briefs that supply a music track, or feeds where the brief asks for high energy.

techniques.name: Long-tailed beat lengths
techniques.summary: Beat lengths follow a long tail instead of an even grid: most beats sit near one median length, a few connective beats snap past at a third of it, and one or two hero beats run about three times as long, so the film never settles into a slideshow rhythm.
techniques.use_when: Launch films and walkthroughs of 15 s or more with eight or more beats, any cut list that came out evenly spaced, and deciding where the hero feature gets its time.
techniques.avoid_when: Polyrhythm loops and fixed-length ask cycles, where equal length is the point; stings under about 8 s, which have too few beats for a distribution; accelerando runs, which set their own length ratios.

techniques.name: One screen direction per act
techniques.summary: Each act owns one direction of travel, so every entrance, exit, drift and camera ramp in it runs the same way, and the direction turns only at an act seam, where the turn itself marks the new chapter.
techniques.use_when: Films built from hard cuts with velocity handoffs, two-act spots (imagery, then type), runs of statements (an upward feed), and vertical films with a rising vector.
techniques.avoid_when: Oners and single camera journeys, where the layout of the surface sets the direction; films whose motion is mostly radial zooms; multi-cell grids; a film with no act change, which should keep one vector throughout.

techniques.name: Machine on the grid, hands off it
techniques.summary: Work the product does (rows inserting, items stacking, text streaming) ticks on a strict metronome, while what a person does (moving the cursor, flipping toggles, clicking) arrives on uneven, deliberating gaps, so the viewer can feel who is acting.
techniques.use_when: Product demos where a person gives an instruction and the product or an agent responds, walkthroughs that mix input with generated output, and any sequence where automation should feel tireless next to a human.
techniques.avoid_when: Pure type films or brand stings with no user in the story; polyrhythm grids, which run their own clocks; musical montages where every event must land on the beat.

techniques.name: Focus ring: pop on click, trim to point
techniques.summary: A thin outline around a control either pops outward and fades the moment it is clicked, or draws itself clockwise around a target and erases from the tail, pointing at the action without a cursor.
techniques.use_when: A click needs a visible result the next shot can build on, or a calm frame must point at the next action without moving a cursor.
techniques.avoid_when: The cursor already sits on the target (the ring is redundant), or the ring would need a glow or blurred halo to read.

techniques.name: In-place character rewrite
techniques.summary: A small monospace status field is overwritten left to right by its new state, or a sensitive value turns to dots and deletes from the right, all inside the same fixed slot with no layout change.
techniques.use_when: The product's own status (sending, receiving, connected) or a privacy claim should change in place and read as the machine's voice.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is decorative rather than real UI status (it becomes filler text), or the field uses a proportional face, so the columns jump.

techniques.name: Anticipation dip before an unlock
techniques.summary: Light builds on a locked card, the card briefly darkens as the lock's shackle swings open, then it pops to clean full-tone content, so the release feels bigger than it is.
techniques.use_when: Something locked, gated or hidden becomes available (an unlock, a reveal, access granted) and the moment should land as a payoff.
techniques.avoid_when: The brightness would clip whites into a bloom, or the film already has two big payoff beats.

techniques.name: One-element tell before the event
techniques.summary: Just before a state change or a cut, exactly one small thing moves, such as a plus glyph turning 45 degrees into an x or an object slowly turning toward its target, while everything else holds.
techniques.use_when: A repeated result cut, or a sudden 2-4 f event, needs anticipation so it reads as caused rather than random.
techniques.avoid_when: Several things already move in the frame (the tell gets lost), or the yaw would leave the rest of the frame static for more than 48 f.

techniques.name: Chip bloom around content
techniques.summary: A container grows out of its content: a dropped icon tile widens into a labelled chip that floods with the accent and wipes back to an outline, or a solid pill swells behind a name so the group becomes a button.
techniques.use_when: An integration, tag or name should become a tangible, clickable object (attached, added, now a button), shown as cause and effect.
techniques.avoid_when: The fill would need several hues to read, or the chip has nothing to do next (a bloom with no follow-up reads as decoration).

techniques.name: Shape handoff: pill becomes the icon
techniques.summary: A labelled capsule empties its text, then collapses at a fixed height into a square tile or circle that becomes the next thing (the app icon, a loader or a dock slot), so the object never disappears, it changes role.
techniques.use_when: A thinking state, prompt or button should hand off to the product identity, or to its new place in the interface, in one continuous take.
techniques.avoid_when: The target shape has nothing to do with the source (the continuity feels arbitrary), or the shot needs a hard cut for rhythm.

techniques.name: Guide cursor: arrive, hover, press
techniques.summary: A cursor travels a bowed path to the element about to act, the target shows its hover state a few frames after the cursor arrives, and a short press triggers the response on the same frame.
techniques.use_when: A person is driving the product, and dense UI needs a point of view that shows the viewer where to look next.
techniques.avoid_when: The product acts on its own, clicks would come faster than one per 30 f, or the shot already has a pointer such as a focus ring.

techniques.name: Velocity-stretch dot
techniques.summary: A small round dot (a cursor or a list marker) stretches into a capsule along its motion in proportion to its speed, anchored at its trailing end, and shrinks back to a dot when it stops.
techniques.use_when: A tiny element must lead the eye across a slab or down a list, and needs speed, direction and character.
techniques.avoid_when: UI truth requires a standard system arrow, or several dots would stretch at once (the trick only reads once).

techniques.name: Shared highlight walks the menu
techniques.summary: One rounded highlight slides from row to row of a sidebar or menu, trailing the cursor, and the chosen row settles into a pale accent tint.
techniques.use_when: Navigation through a menu, sidebar or list should read as a small human decision, with spatial continuity.
techniques.avoid_when: The rows are too small to read at the shot's framing (push in first), or a soft radial bloom would be added to the highlight.

techniques.name: Stretchy tab indicator
techniques.summary: The selected pill of a segmented control shoots to the new option with its leading edge arriving first, stretches to about 1.9x its width mid-travel, then hugs the new label as the label takes the active colour.
techniques.use_when: A tab, filter or toggle switch causes the next state (the chart changes, the list swaps) and deserves weight.
techniques.avoid_when: The control has more than about five options in a tight row (the stretch overlaps its neighbours), or the indicator would only read with refraction or a frosted backdrop behind it.

techniques.name: Radial dash burst around a word
techniques.summary: Short dashes burst outward around a hero word on the beat, drift almost imperceptibly while it is read, then fly outward faster as the frame pushes into the cut.
techniques.use_when: A single hero word on a beat needs a physical punch.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is body copy, the shot is UI, or the burst has already been used once in the film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the random dashes with 12 evenly spaced radial ticks (every 30 degrees, 20 px long, 3 px stroke, C.ink, one SVG) forming an ordered ring around the word. Drive them with the same radius curve: 187 to 274 px in 16 f E.out, a 0.5 px/f drift, then out to about 450 px over the last 20 f E.in. It reads as a graphic emphasis mark rather than debris. A single 2 px ring stroke on the same curve also works.

techniques.name: Launch hop that never lands
techniques.summary: A centred app icon hops up as if launching, hangs at the top for a beat and starts to fall, and the camera leaves before it lands, so the hop motivates the scene change.
techniques.use_when: Opening the app or launching a feature should motivate the move to the next scene with a familiar OS gesture.
techniques.avoid_when: The icon must come to rest in the same shot (then it needs a real landing), or several icons would hop in turn.

techniques.name: Two-beat confirm cascade
techniques.summary: A row of buttons or toggles confirms one by one: the label or knob changes first, the fill follows a beat later, and the rows go at uneven, human gaps.
techniques.use_when: Several integrations, permissions or capabilities switch on, and each confirmation must stay legible at video speed.
techniques.avoid_when: There is only one control (use the press envelope), or every row would start at the same interval.

techniques.name: Spinner resolves to a check
techniques.summary: A working indicator (a rotating dashed ring in a step list, or a small spinning disc pushed into the middle of a sentence) turns into a check with a short tag the moment the step is done.
techniques.use_when: The product works through steps on its own (an agent, a sync, an import), and each completion should land as a small lock.
techniques.avoid_when: There is a single long wait with nothing resolving (show progress instead), or all the checks would resolve on one frame.

techniques.name: Send as a ghosted handoff
techniques.summary: On send, the composer's text drifts up and fades away while the same content appears above as a posted message, briefly overlapping the old text, instead of flying between containers.
techniques.use_when: A message, prompt or post is submitted and the result appears elsewhere in the same frame; this is calmer and cheaper than a flight.
techniques.avoid_when: The journey itself is the point (show the flight), or the move would serve as a transition between shots, where a crossfade is never the default.

techniques.name: Drag, lift and seat
techniques.summary: A chip or file picked up by the cursor lifts off the surface, follows the hand with a slight lag and tilt, then drops into its slot with a small contact squash as the slot accepts it.
techniques.use_when: A drag-and-drop (attach a file, add an integration, reorder a card) causes the next state.
techniques.avoid_when: The drag path is long (over about 600 px, cut it), or the item contains text that must be read while it tilts.

techniques.name: Badge count bump
techniques.summary: A notification badge or counter chip ticks up: the digit rolls to the next value while the badge gives a small pulse, once per increment.
techniques.use_when: Incoming activity (messages, leads, approvals) should register as small, countable events on the UI.
techniques.avoid_when: The count is the hero number of the shot (use a full counter), or increments would come faster than about one per 12 f.

techniques.name: Click to focus: I-beam, ring, caret
techniques.summary: An arrow cursor turns into an I-beam as it enters an empty field and clicks. The field's border sharpens, a caret appears and blinks twice at an uneven, human pace, and on the first key the placeholder vanishes and the pointer fades away.
techniques.use_when: A shot opens on an empty prompt, search or chat field and the first action is typing into it, so the click into the field becomes the cause of everything after.
techniques.avoid_when: The field is already focused or pre-filled, the product acts on its own with no cursor, or the film has already played the full two-blink wait once (later prompts start at the first key).

techniques.name: Cursor glyph follows context
techniques.summary: The pointer changes shape with what it is over, as a real system pointer does: an I-beam over text, an open hand over something draggable, a closed fist while dragging, and the arrow everywhere else. Each change is a one-frame swap.
techniques.use_when: A cursor drives a walkthrough that both types and drags, and the pointer must behave like the real system's rather than an arrow stamped on everything.
techniques.avoid_when: The cursor only clicks buttons (the arrow is correct there), or a snappy vertical edit would flash the glyph changes past before they read.

techniques.name: Drag-select snaps glyph by glyph
techniques.summary: An I-beam presses at the start of a phrase and drags across it, a tinted highlight grows behind the text one whole character at a time, and on release a small action bar grows out of the selection, ready for the product to act on it.
techniques.use_when: The product acts on a piece of text the user picks (rewrite, translate, comment, format, ask about a passage), and the pick should read as a human choice rather than a preset.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is under about 40 px tall at the shot's framing (push in first), the range spans more than two lines, or the cursor never touches text anywhere else in the film.

techniques.name: Card fan that buries, then scatters
techniques.summary: A dozen identical cards swoop in from two corners along a curved arc and stack in depth until they bury the frame. They drift for a beat, then scatter outward and leave one small card in the centre that carries the number.
techniques.use_when: A big count or scale claim (cards issued, transactions, users) needs to feel physical before it collapses to one legible number.
techniques.avoid_when: The film already has a card or tile swarm, or the stat must be read at once; in a calm film the 50 f bury is too loud.

techniques.name: Pinned label over a swapping world
techniques.summary: A pin pops on a 3D-rendered place and a short data tag on a leader line tracks that point as the camera orbits. On a cut, the world underneath switches between 3D and flat while the tag holds its screen position.
techniques.use_when: Location or geography matters ('this happens in a real place'), or a flat diagram should be revealed as a real object, and back.
techniques.avoid_when: There is no real 3D plate or scene to anchor to; a tag floating over a flat screenshot gains nothing from projection.

techniques.name: Tilted object on a spotlit ground
techniques.summary: A real card or device lies in perspective on a dark surface under one soft pool of light. Most of the frame falls to black, and a slow drift slides the light across the object's face.
techniques.use_when: A single notification, card or device should feel like an object in a room, not on a slide, especially in a dark, low-key film.
techniques.avoid_when: The same act already tilts things on this axis, or the film is bright and flat; never on a bare screenshot without ground and shadow.

techniques.name: Depth orbit ring that collapses into the mark
techniques.summary: Small icons orbit the central mark on a tilted ellipse: they grow and pass in front as they come near and shrink behind it as they go far. Then the ring speeds up and contracts into the mark.
techniques.use_when: Showing an ecosystem of integrations or inputs around one core in about 1.5 s, without words.
techniques.avoid_when: The icons must be read or named, or the film already used an orbit; more than 8 icons turns into noise.

techniques.name: Folded channel that unfolds flat
techniques.summary: A wide card starts bent into a U-shaped channel with its side walls folded toward camera. It flattens open while the cards stacked inside fan out into a neat row, then the whole thing tips away.
techniques.use_when: Revealing a list, a set of plans or a stack of items as a tangible moment, not a flat fade-up.
techniques.avoid_when: The same act already uses a vertical-hinge yaw, or the contents are dense text that must be read during the unfold.

techniques.name: 3D flip that swaps state
techniques.summary: An icon or card turns over in 3D and comes back around changed (outline to solid, grey to full colour), then shrinks and travels to its next place.
techniques.use_when: A state change (activated, connected, colourised) needs a physical cause, especially as the film's only 3D turn.
techniques.avoid_when: Several flips have already happened, or the cards carry heavy text (it goes mirrored and soft mid-turn).

techniques.name: Peek, hover, launch and recede
techniques.summary: A device or product panel barely rises from the bottom edge, pauses, then shoots up to centre. It is tipped back as it rises, faces camera as it arrives, and slowly settles away from camera.
techniques.use_when: Introducing hardware or a hero product surface, where anticipation makes the main move feel powerful.
techniques.avoid_when: The film has already used anticipation twice, or the object is small UI (it reads as a bounce).

techniques.name: Edge-on sliver snaps face-on
techniques.summary: A thin edge-on sliver snaps open into a full face-on coin or badge. Most of the turn happens in the first frame, then it eases into place as its face catches the light.
techniques.use_when: Revealing a token, coin, badge or mark decisively, or turning a physical object into the logo at the close.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat UI icons without thickness (the edge-on frame becomes an invisible line), or the film already has several flips.

techniques.name: Product on a thick extruded slab
techniques.summary: The live interface sits on the front of a thick matte slab with rounded corners. When the camera orbits or yaws, the slab's solid edge appears, which turns a screen into an object and makes every angle readable.
techniques.use_when: A single-take product walkthrough or a feature film where the camera travels across one interface.
techniques.avoid_when: The film is flat 2D throughout, or the camera never yaws (the edge never shows and the build is wasted).

techniques.name: Impact morph with stretch and floor ripple
techniques.summary: Something accelerates into a 3D tile. On contact the tile swaps shape and colour in one frame, stretches tall and settles without rebound while the floor beneath it ripples.
techniques.use_when: Cause and effect is the message: raw input hits the product and becomes something new.
techniques.avoid_when: The film has already spent its two true landings or is calm; never as a generic transition.

techniques.name: Icon lifts out of its row into a 3D hero
techniques.summary: A small icon tile peels out of a settings row and inverts from dark to light. It flies to frame centre growing almost 2x, tilted in 3D and slowly turning as it floats into the next chapter.
techniques.use_when: A tiny detail (an integration, a setting, a source) should become the hero of the next section, bridging two chapters.
techniques.avoid_when: The icon has no follow-up role, or another element already did a lift-to-centre in this film.

techniques.name: Cube turn to a blank face
techniques.summary: Words converge and slide under an icon, then the icon turns 90 degrees like a cube to show a plain accent face that becomes the field for what comes next.
techniques.use_when: Clearing a sentence into a single colour field or a seed for the logo with a clean geometric gesture.
techniques.avoid_when: The tile carries fine detail (it shears during the turn), or the same element was already flipped.

techniques.name: Press tilt that hides a swap
techniques.summary: A card tips in 3D toward the point that was clicked or tapped and relaxes back flat. The content changes on the tilt's peak frame, so the change has a physical cause.
techniques.use_when: Clicks, copies, likes and swaps in a UI walkthrough that need tactility without a flash.
techniques.avoid_when: Every click in the film already tilts (use it for 1-3 key presses), or the target is a tiny chip where the tilt cannot be seen.

techniques.name: Exploded layer stack
techniques.summary: A live UI component turns to a three-quarter view and separates into its layers along depth to show how it is built, then snaps back together and turns flat.
techniques.use_when: Explaining what a product is made of (data, logic, interface), or that one surface stacks several capabilities.
techniques.avoid_when: The component is visually thin (the layers look identical), or the act's axis is already yaw.
